title: Cost Control Agent: Safe Apply Strategy and Surge Simulation Postmortem
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
A weekend rollout of the Optimize cost-control agent introduced an aggressive batching/cache recommendation profile that produced an unexpected token-surge for a subset of long-tail request patterns. The system applied candidate parameters automatically to a canary pool, but the canary config propagated to a larger reserved pool due to a bug in the staged-apply coordinator. The result was elevated end-to-end latency and a brief increase in downstream timeout errors for 0.6% of production traffic for ~45 minutes. No data was lost.

Impact:
- Affected traffic: ~0.6% of user requests (spiky distribution across 3 customer tenants)
- Duration: 45 minutes peak, 2.5 hours to fully stabilize as caches warmed and a rollback finished
- Symptoms: elevated tail latency (p95->p99+200ms), transient 504 errors from gateway on long-sequence generation requests, increased token counts per request for some prompt shapes
- Customer impact: medium (timeout-sensitive features degraded for a small number of customers)

Timeline (abridged):
- 2025-02-16 03:12 UTC: Optimize agent scheduled parameter apply to canary pool (dry-run signals OK)
- 2025-02-16 03:18 UTC: Staged-apply coordinator unexpectedly propagated profile to reserved pool due to missing guard check (bug introduced in engineer patch ENG-12200)
- 2025-02-16 03:30 UTC: First alerts for elevated tail latency; on-call paging triggered
- 2025-02-16 04:05 UTC: Manual stop applied; backfill rollback queued
- 2025-02-16 05:00 UTC: Rollback completed for majority of nodes; mitigation scripts triggered to flush warmup anomalies
- 2025-02-16 06:45 UTC: Metrics returned to baseline; follow-up monitoring active

Root cause analysis:
1) Staged-apply coordinator lacked an explicit canary separation enforcement. A race condition allowed the canary token to be accepted by the global rollout orchestrator when topology reconciliation happened during a node restart.
2) The Optimize agent's recommendation engine produced an aggressive derate factor for batching that increased grouping across long sequences, which in turn caused unexpected KV cache thrash for certain prompt prefixes.
3) The safety gate that compares dry-run cost delta vs. observed latency regression was configured with a loose threshold (5%) that was insufficient for long-tail sequences.
4) Automated rollback logic relies on a single success metric (apply_ack) which did not reflect downstream latency degradations.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Reverted the staged-apply coordinator changes (hotfix PR #GH-3312) and applied explicit canary-to-global boundary checks.
- Triggered emergency feature flag to disable automatic global expansion of Optimize recommendations.
- Deployed a short-term throttle that limits candidate batch-size increases to +10% per 10m per pool.
- Manually flushed affected KV caches and triggered a controlled cache-warmup job for the reserved pool.

Longer-term recommendations (playbook-level):
A) Coordinator & rollout hardening:
   - Add explicit canary tokens and enforcement: a coordinator must verify canary_id != global_id before any global apply.
   - Introduce a two-phase commit with quorum checks across pool managers for staged applies.
B) Safety metric expansion:
   - Expand the gating surface: include p99 latency, 5xx rates, token-per-request delta, and cache-miss-rate in the safety gate rather than relying on a single cost signal.
   - Use dynamic thresholds: long-tail sequences get stricter latency regression bounds (default 2%).
C) Simulation & verification:
   - Build a surge-simulation harness that replays a corpus of long-sequence prompt traces against candidate parameter sets to surface cache thrash and worst-case latency before apply.
   - Require successful dry-run validation against the surge harness for any candidate with >15% estimated token delta.
D) Safe-apply features:
   - Staged ramp-up with derate factors: enforce a max per-interval parameter change (derate factor) tied to observed cache-miss signals.
   - Apply dry-run shadowing: run candidate config in shadow on 10% of requests for 1 hour and evaluate.
E) Rollback & observability:
   - Define rollback safepoints tied to stable-save markers; rollback should trigger cache-warmup jobs automatically to avoid cold-start spikes.
   - Add per-parameter telemetry and time-series dashboards for quick root cause isolation.

Testing & verification plan:
- Unit tests for coordinator boundary checks; e2e tests in CI that simulate canary->global race scenarios.
- Integrate surge-simulation harness into PR gating for Optimize engine changes.
- Create synthetic regression tests that assert p99 and 5xx bounds for long-sequence corpus under candidate configs.

Rollout checklist for proposed changes:
1) Implement coordinator harden + unit tests (owner: infra-runtimes)
2) Deploy to staging + run surge-simulation for top-10 customers' trace corpus (owner: optimize-team)
3) Shadow apply for 10% traffic for 2 hours; observe safety metrics (owner: SRE)
4) If safe, canary apply to 5% reserved capacity for 12 hours with automated rollback gates (owner: oncall)
5) Gradual expansion with telemetry audit every step

Follow-ups / action items (owners):
- ENG-12841: Add canary enforcement tests and fix race (owner: Marcus Nguyen, estimate: 3)
- ENG-12842: Surge-simulation harness design doc and PoC (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 5)
- ENG-12843: Expand safety gates to include p99/5xx/token-delta/cache-miss (owner: Observability team, estimate: 4)
- ENG-12844: Implement rollback safepoints + cache-warmup automation (owner: Infra SRE, estimate: 5)
- Run a post-deployment customer verification pass for top-10 tenants (owner: CS & SRE)

Notes & Links:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/3312
- Canary logs snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/optimize/canary-20250216
- Incident runbook used: https://confluence.redwood.company/x/Optimize-Incident-Runbook

Conclusion:
This incident exposed two orthogonal weaknesses: the staged-apply coordination logic and insufficient safety gate breadth for long-tail sequences. The recommended playbook combines stronger enforcement at the coordinator level, a richer safety metric set, and a pre-apply surge-simulation step that will materially reduce the risk of cache-thrash induced latency surges. The proposed follow-ups are scoped, prioritized, and owner-assigned above.
